article.title: Why Revenue per Customer Can Rise After Low-Spending Customers Leave

paragraphs.en:
Revenue per customer can rise even when existing customers do not spend more. This happens because an average depends not only on individual behavior but also on who remains in the population.

Imagine 100 customers. Fifty high-spending customers each spend $200, while fifty low-spending customers each spend $50. Total revenue is $12,500, so revenue per customer is $125. Next year, suppose all high-spending customers remain and still spend $200, but twenty low-spending customers leave. The remaining 80 customers generate $11,500. Total revenue falls, yet revenue per customer rises to $143.75. Nobody increased spending.

This is a customer-mix effect. Removing low-value observations mechanically raises the average of the remaining population. A dashboard showing only ARPU or average annual spend might therefore create an optimistic story: ‘Customer value improved.’ In reality, the business lost customers and revenue.

The reverse can happen during successful acquisition. A company may attract many new customers who are still early in their lifecycle and have not had enough time to spend much. Revenue per customer can fall even while total revenue, customer count, and long-term growth prospects improve.

A better analysis separates full-population performance from same-customer behavior. First, report total customers, total revenue, and revenue per customer. Second, split customers into retained, new, and churned groups. Third, compare spending for customers observed in both periods. This common-customer view answers whether continuing customers actually changed their spending.

Exposure time also matters. A customer acquired in the final month of a twelve-month period should not automatically be compared with someone observed for the full year. Depending on the question, analysts can align observation windows or calculate monthly spend while clearly documenting the denominator.

Segment movement is another useful check. If the share of low-spending customers shrinks while the high-spending share grows, ask why. Did low-value customers churn? Did customers genuinely move upward? Did a data filter change? These mechanisms have different business implications.

Language in the final report should match the evidence. ‘Revenue per customer increased’ is a descriptive fact. ‘Customers are spending more’ is a behavioral claim and requires stronger evidence. A safer statement might be: ‘Average revenue per active customer increased, but part of the increase reflects the loss of lower-spending customers.’

This distinction matters for strategy. Selective churn can make averages look healthier while weakening the customer base. Conversely, rapid acquisition can temporarily dilute averages while building future value. Good analysis therefore keeps totals, averages, population composition, and within-customer changes visible at the same time.
paragraphs.zh:
每客營收上升，不代表既有顧客真的花更多。平均值同時受到個人行為與母體組成影響。假設原本高消費與低消費顧客各 50 人；第二年高消費者完全沒增加支出，但部分低消費者流失，總營收甚至下降，每客營收仍可能上升。這就是 customer-mix effect。

反過來，成功大量獲取新客時，新客因觀察期間短、生命週期尚早，可能拉低平均值，即使總營收與顧客數都在成長。因此分析要同時看全體表現與 same-customer behavior，拆分 retained、new、churned customers，並處理 exposure time。

報告用語也要和證據一致。「Revenue per customer increased」只是描述事實；「Customers are spending more」則是行為因果式解讀，需要共同顧客等更強證據。選擇性流失可能讓平均數變漂亮卻削弱客群，因此 totals、averages、population mix 與 within-customer change 應一起呈現。
paragraphs.ja:
顧客一人当たり売上が上昇しても、既存顧客の支出が増えたとは限りません。平均値は個人行動だけでなく、誰が母集団に残っているかにも左右されます。低支出顧客が多く離脱すれば、残存顧客の支出が変わらなくても平均は機械的に上昇します。

逆に、新規獲得が急増すると、観測期間の短い新規顧客が平均を押し下げることがあります。そのため全体の顧客数・売上・一人当たり売上に加え、継続・新規・離脱を分け、共通顧客の支出変化も確認します。観測期間の違いにも注意が必要です。

「一人当たり売上が上昇した」は記述的事実ですが、「顧客が以前より多く使うようになった」は行動変化の主張です。低単価層の選択的な離脱で平均が改善している可能性もあるため、総量、平均、構成、同一顧客の変化をセットで説明することが重要です。

vocabulary.usage: Total revenue fell despite higher revenue per customer.
The average rises mechanically when low spenders leave.
Separate churned customers from retained customers.
Selective churn can improve an average artificially.

business.term: Let's separate the mix effect from same-customer change.
business.explanation: 區分客群構成變化與同一顧客的行為變化。

business.term: The average improved, but the underlying customer base shrank.
business.explanation: 提醒平均 KPI 變好不代表整體 business health 改善。
